introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2023. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators are allowed. Formulae booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.
incertitudes: Q5(c) : le graphique est a tracer par le candidat ; le corrige le decrit (droites, hachures, sommets (4,0), (10,0), (8,4), (4,2)). « Minimum number of books and pens » est ambigu : lu comme le plus petit couple possible avec au moins un stylo (4 livres, 1 stylo) ; si zero stylo etait permis, la reponse serait 4 livres et 0 stylo.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Eposi has only 6,000 FCFA to buy her books and pens. She buys $x$ books for 600 FCFA each and $y$ pens for 300 FCFA each.

(a) Write down the total cost in terms of $x$ and $y$ of these materials and hence show that $2x+y\le20$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cost of $x$ books $=600x$ FCFA; cost of $y$ pens $=300y$ FCFA.

Total cost $=600x+300y$ FCFA.

She has only $6{,}000$ FCFA, so the total cost cannot exceed it:

$$600x+300y\le6000.$$

Divide every term by $300$:

$$2x+y\le20.\quad\text{(shown)}$$

**Total cost $=600x+300y$, hence $2x+y\le20$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
She intended to buy at least 4 books and decided to buy more than twice as many books as pens.

(b) Write down further two inequalities involving $x$ and $y$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
- "At least 4 books" means the number of books is $4$ or more: $x\ge4$.
- "More than twice as many books as pens" means the number of books is strictly greater than twice the number of pens: $x>2y$.

**$x\ge4$ and $x>2y$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) On a graph paper, using the scale 2 cm to represent 2 units on the $x$-axis and 2 cm to represent 4 units on the $y$-axis, shade, so as to leave unshaded, the region satisfied by these three inequalities and hence determine the minimum number of books and pens she buys. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Scale.** On the $x$-axis $1$ cm represents $1$ unit; on the $y$-axis $1$ cm represents $2$ units.

**Boundary lines.**

- $2x+y=20$ (solid line) passes through $(0,20)$ and $(10,0)$; the region wanted is below it ($0+0\le20$ is true at the origin).
- $x=4$ (solid vertical line); the region wanted is on the right of it ($x\ge4$).
- $x=2y$, i.e. $y=\dfrac x2$ (**dashed** line, because the inequality is strict) passes through $(0,0)$, $(4,2)$ and $(8,4)$; the region wanted is below it ($4>0$ is true at the point $(4,0)$ in the region).

Also $y\ge0$ (she cannot buy a negative number of pens). Shade the parts of the paper that do **not** satisfy the inequalities, so that the wanted region stays unshaded.

**Wanted region.** It is the quadrilateral with vertices $(4,0)$, $(10,0)$, $(8,4)$ [intersection of $y=\frac x2$ and $2x+y=20$: $2x+\frac x2=20\Rightarrow x=8$] and $(4,2)$ [on the dashed line, not included].

**Minimum.** The numbers of books and pens are whole numbers and she buys both books and pens, so $y\ge1$. The smallest number of books is $x=4$; with $x=4$ the condition $x>2y$ gives $y<2$, so $y=1$. The point $(4,1)$ lies in the unshaded region: $4\ge4$, $4>2\times1$ and $2(4)+1=9\le20$.

**She buys a minimum of 4 books and 1 pen (5 items in all).**
